comment: I expected DSST 389 to be the most difficult DSST course I'd take at UR, but the opposite was true. Our class was basically all seniors, so Dr. Arnold didn't push us extremely hard after the first exam. Most of the course was introducing various topics, without getting super in-depth. HW and exams were very chill.

This might just be because my class fully consisted of seniors, but Dr Arnold didn't expect much of us at all. The "homework" was maximum reading 3 screens worth of his online textbook (great resource, btw) and doing a short little activity after. He's a super chill grader and you can often leave class early.

Take Dr. Arnold for DSST289 and/or DSST389 if you can!! He is the best professor! He provides study guides with exactly what will be on the exams, and lectures consist of him talking, but also working on an in-class notebook, so it is a nice mix. Also, very little homework!

This is the second DSST course I've taken with Dr. Arnold, and he is truly the best prof to take...especially if you aren't a math/CS person. I took this course as a humanities double major, and I did just fine by doing the readings and paying attention in class. Super caring and kind professor who wants to see you succeed.

Did DSST289 and DSST389 with him. Very clear exam outlines that are easy to study for. In class coding notebooks that are based off the readings (which arent always necessary to do beforehand). Super nice and funny, some of the content can be confusing just due to the complexity of it but he explains it well and has clear expectations!

Very Informative class, very little out-of-class work (short readings and completing in-class work for practice), exam expectations are VERY clearly laid out, same with the Final project, which takes the place of the exam and is easy. 10/10 class.
Also, the prof has an adorable little dog that he may bring to class towards the end of the semester.

Dr. Arnold has a great personality. His readings before class (notes that he wrote himself) were super helpful. His tests and the final project were not hard. Great class for an intro to data science. No prior coding experience is required. It was an easier class compared with other ones I was taking but you can learn a lot. Highly recommend!

The class is super helpful no matter what you major in. If you've never done coding, there might be a bit of a learning curve, but you will catch up quickly. Exams are easy and test exactly what you've learned. Dr. Arnold is helpful and provides good feedback. He is also good at explaining harder concepts and putting it into practice. Great class!

Dr. Arnold is great! He always tries to explain the concepts in simpler terms so that everyone can understand, and normally uses examples to make things clear. The class is project-based, which I really liked, and there is a short final self-reflection at the end of the semester.

Awesome guy, great class. Dr. Arnold's statistical modeling class would be useful for literally anybody, and it's honestly not difficult. Most of the classwork is very fun, the lectures are quick and to the point, and the professor is just fun to listen to. The tests aren't hard, and the projects are both helpful and meaningful. Great class, 10/10!

Crazy smart, incredibly friendly, used to be the polar bear mascot at Bowdoin. He explains things so clearly and caters classes to be interesting for both the math-y and CS-y groups. Projects were super fun. Classes were structured as working thru tutorials, which you could take as far as you'd like. Super reasonable grader.
HE IS A REAL GEM! He is so smart, knowledgeable, straightforward, and helpful!
Enjoyable class, average amount of homework. He cares about both the Students and the course content.
A great professor. Really knowledgable about subject areas, gave clear guidelines and made class interesting!
Dr. Arnold's grading criteria is super confusing. The major grades are the three projects and it is not really clear what he wants in these projects.
